title: decaying-frequency sliding-window eviction + prefix quotas and safe reclamation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: As continuous batching increases concurrent prefix diversity and live KV usage, simple LRU or fixed TTL approaches cause either unfair eviction of low-volume but latency-sensitive prefixes or premature reclamation that breaks in-flight batches. Proposal: implement a decaying-frequency sliding-window (DF-SW) eviction algorithm combined with per-prefix soft-quotas and an epoched safe-reclamation protocol that coordinates with the batching runtime to avoid KV miss regressions. Also add light-weight slab compaction heuristics to reduce GPU fragmentation and improve reclaim efficiency.
technical_decisions: Eviction algorithm: DF-SW maintains a fixed-size time window (configurable, default 30s) with sub-window buckets where each lookup increments a decayed count. Evict by lowest decayed-frequency across the window, not pure LRU.

Prefix quotas: assign soft memory quotas per prefix namespace (configurable hierarchy: tenant -> model -> route). When overall pressure hits thresholds, evictions first reduce over-capacity prefixes respecting soft quotas to prevent starving low-traffic prefixes.

Safe reclamation: coordinate with continuous-batching runtime using 'reclamation epochs' exposed via per-batch markers. Items are only reclaimed after the reclaim-epoch is acknowledged by the batching runtime to be free of references.

Slab compaction: introduce compaction hints (small/medium/large slots) and a background compaction pass that avoids blocking serving threads; compaction is heuristically triggered when fragmentation > 18%.

Metrics and monotonicity invariants: define hit-rate and per-prefix warmness. Guarantee: once a prefix's warmness surpasses the warmed threshold, the DF-SW monotonicity property ensures eviction probability does not increase for a short stabilization period (configurable) unless explicitly over-quota.
Fallbacks: on memory emergency, fall back to TTL-based coarse reclamation with prioritized prefix whitelist to reduce customer-visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype pushed and merged to feature branch with unit tests and integration tests (PR link in 'links').
On perf-3 cluster, DF-SW improves median inter-prefix miss-rate for low-volume prefixes by >= 25% vs baseline LRU at equivalent memory pressure.
No increase in tail latency (p95 generation latency) beyond 3% in steady workloads; bursts allowed up to 7% with documented mitigation steps.
Safe-reclamation correctness validated by shadow-run harness: no KV read-after-free observed across 10k simulated overlapping batch traces.
Slab compaction does not introduce blocking GC pauses > 5ms on the critical path under normal load.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (prototype): implement DF-SW counters and per-prefix accounting inside runtime allocator; add feature flag 'dfsw_eviction_v1'.
Phase 2 (coordination): add reclamation epoch markers to batching runtime SPI and wire host->runtime ack channel (gRPC).
Phase 3 (optimizations): slab compaction pass, fragmentation metric, and admin config knobs for quotas and window length.
Phase 4 (hardening): run chaos/fuzzbench with synthetic prefix churn, run end-to-end canary against internal chat demo, collect metrics for three full days before ramp.
Important: keep default global config conservative to reduce blast radius; enable for selected tenant cohorts first.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created; initial design sketch and trade-offs discussed in eng-arch sync.
2026-03-03: Prototype algorithm implemented in local runtime shim; accuracy validated with offline trace replay (10M ops).
2026-03-05: Design review with PM and DX: agreed on prefix soft-quotas and stabilization window parameters.
2026-03-10: PR #12567 opened with DF-SW counters and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12567.

2026-03-12: Integration test harness added; preliminary perf runs on perf-3 show 28% improvement for cold prefixes at 85% memory pressure; raising status to In Progress and starting epoch coordination work.
test_plan: Unit tests: eviction ordering determinism under synthetic sequences, per-prefix accounting tests.
Integration: shadow-run against live batching runtime with cross-checks for read-after-free, using 10k overlapping batch traces.
Perf: compare DF-SW vs LRU and TTL baselines at memory pressures (60%, 80%, 95%) across three workload classes (uniform, long-tail prefixes, extreme-tail microservices).
Fuzz: run kv-eviction-fuzzbench (extended scenario) for 72 hours with randomized prefetch/pin/unpin sequences.
Canary: enable feature flag for 5% of traffic on staging tenants, run 72-hour canary then 10% production for 48 hours before ramping.
rollout_plan: Stage gated rollout controlled by feature flag 'dfsw_eviction_v1' and 'reclamation_epoch_v1'.
Start: internal-staging (team infra) for smoke. Monitor hit-rate, tail latency, and reclamation ack lag metrics.
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks depending on metrics and no regressions.
Rollback: toggle off feature flag and run global TTL-emergency path if read-after-free or large tail latency observed.
Post-rollout: schedule a 1-week observability burn to collect long-tail regressions and tune soft-quotas.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: coordination protocol lag could delay reclamation and increase memory pressure. Mitigation: set bounded wait and fall back to conservative TTL reclamation under sustained lag.
Risk: misconfiguration of quotas could starve important prefixes. Mitigation: start with tenant-level defaults and provide rollout monitoring + auto-suggest quotas via Optimize heuristics.
Risk: slab compaction may contend with allocator. Mitigation: offload compaction to low-priority background worker and throttle based on CPU/GPU utilization.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on correctness-first approach; later follow-ups will explore machine-learning-driven quota tuning and per-tenant adaptive window sizing.
